prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” roofing company for everyone — the right choice depends on your budget, roof type, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and how much warranty/service you want. I can help find top local options if you give your ZIP or address. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to pick the best Dallas roofing contractor for your replacement.

How to choose the right company
- Verify insurance and business status: confirm current general liability and workers’ comp insurance (get certificates). Note: Texas has no statewide roofing license, so insurance, local registrations/permits, and references matter more.
- Check reputation: read Google, Yelp, Angi, BBB, Nextdoor reviews; ask for 3 local references with similar jobs.
- Confirm warranties: get both manufacturer (shingle) and contractor workmanship warranty in writing, with length and transferability.
- Experience and certifications: look for GAF/IKO/CertainTeed/Atlas certified installers if you want shingle manufacturer warranties honored.
- Written, itemized estimate: must show materials, labor, permit costs, disposal, timeline, and payment schedule. Compare at least 3 estimates.
- Permits and cleanup: contractor should obtain permits and remove old roofing and debris (ask about driveway protection and magnet sweep).
- Payment terms: avoid large upfront balances (typical is a modest deposit with remainder on completion). Be cautious with full-cash, high-pressure deals.
- Storm-chaser warning: avoid companies that appeared after a storm, offer to start immediately door-to-door, or pressure you to sign on the spot.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you insured? Can I see a COI naming me as additional insured?
- How long have you been in business locally?
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?
- Do you use subcontractors? Who will supervise the job?
- What brands and warranties do you offer?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and photos of completed work?
- What is the projected start date and job duration?
- How do you handle change orders or unseen damage?

Red flags
- No insurance/reluctant to provide COI
- Only takes cash or demands full payment up front
- No written contract or vague scope
- Door-to-door salespeople after storms
- Extremely low bids far below competitors

Where to look for reputable Dallas roofers
- Google Maps and reviews
- BBB (Dallas/Fort Worth)
- Angi/HomeAdvisor
- Yelp and Nextdoor
- Local Facebook homeowner groups
- Ask neighbors or HOA for recent replacements

If you want, I can:
- Pull together 3–5 highly rated Dallas roofing contractors near you (need ZIP or neighborhood), or
- Review estimates or contracts you receive and point out concerns.

Which would you prefer? If you want local recommendations, tell me your ZIP code, whether the project is residential or commercial, roof type (asphalt shingle, metal, tile), and whether you’re working with insurance.
